observed_rotation.inferred_label: Corn-Soybean, no cover crop; reduced tillage

corn.detection: This field's own green cover in its 5 CDL corn years (2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024): median of 298 clear Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 observations, +-8 day window.

soybean.detection: This field's own green cover in its 5 CDL soybean years (2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025): median of 367 clear Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 observations, +-8 day window.

cereal_rye.detection: 9 corn/soybean fields within 6 km (USDA CDL) whose Sentinel-2 NDVI median was >= 0.35 between 21 Mar and 5 May, before any cash crop emerges -- 9 of 841 field-springs screened, 2018-2021; one curve per field-season from 376 clear observations, median across fields, kept from the post-harvest low (DOY 317) to the spring termination low (DOY 154). CDL does not label cover crops; in Iowa a spring-green winter cover is overwhelmingly cereal rye.

uncertainty.reason: NASA POWER is gridded reanalysis at ~0.5 deg (roughly 50 km), not a weather station. Checked against Story County, Iowa station normals over 2000-2024 it runs about +1.0 C warm, which inflates growing degree days by roughly 12% and makes the frost-free season about a week longer than it really is.
uncertainty.affects: Treat marginal cover crops -- ones that only just reach establishment before frost -- as not proven. Check your own last-frost date with your extension office before seeding.

uncertainty.reason: Rainfall erosivity is properly measured from 30-minute storm intensity (EI30). We approximate it from daily rainfall with a power law whose coefficients are not calibrated for Iowa, so the absolute value in MJ.mm/ha/h is uncertain. Because the coefficient enters as a multiplier, the RANKING of rotations and the percentage differences between them are unaffected.
uncertainty.affects: Trust the comparison between rotations. Do not quote the absolute erosivity number without saying it is an uncalibrated estimate.

uncertainty.reason: This is a modelled single-layer bucket water balance driven by NASA POWER rainfall and Hargreaves reference ET -- not a measurement. We chose it over SMAP because SMAP is 9-11 km, so one pixel would cover roughly 1,500 fields this size. The model ignores runoff, drainage, soil texture and rooting depth.
uncertainty.affects: Use it only as a coarse go/no-go on whether a seeding window is plausibly moist. Never read it as your field's actual moisture.

uncertainty.reason: Iowa loses most winter satellite scenes to cloud and snow, so mid-winter cover rests on far fewer observations.
uncertainty.affects: Trust the grayed-out arcs less than the summer ones.

uncertainty.reason: Residue cover comes from the NDTI tillage index scaled between two endmembers: bare soil 0.009 / full residue 0.190, the 5th and 95th percentiles of mean NDTI over 213 nearby corn/soybean fields (1607 post-planting and 4658 post-harvest field-scenes, dry dates, non-green pixels). No residue transects were measured on this farm; moisture and soil colour shift NDTI. Shifting both endmembers by +-0.02 moves this field from 110 to 40-203 bare days. Readings use only non-green pixels on dates with <= 3 mm of NASA POWER rain in the prior two days.
uncertainty.affects: Read the edges of the autumn and spring gaps as approximate, not to the day.

uncertainty.reason: The cover-crop curve is measured, not modelled: the median of 9 nearby fields that were green before planting. CDL does not label cover crops, so a few of those fields could carry winter weeds or volunteer grain instead of a seeded cover.
uncertainty.affects: Expect a real rye stand on this farm to land within the spread of its neighbours, not on the median.

uncertainty.reason: These are satellite phenology dates: green-up onset trails planting by about three to four weeks, and the end of senescence comes one to three weeks before harvest.
uncertainty.affects: Use them for timing the season, not as the farm's operation dates.
